target_customer: Medical schools and other healthcare education programs (and their students) that pay per seat for exam prep and cohort analytics
problem: Healthcare students fail or leave programs because study resources are generic, and faculty lack early signals on which students need help.
business_model: B2B annual per-seat licenses to schools plus student study tools
product_category: Edtech, AI precision education for healthcare (formerly Synaptiq)

founders.name: Ryan Phelps
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: MD, previously a neurosurgery resident at Stanford and a medical student at UCSF.

founders.name: Kevin Bastoul
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: software engineer at Block and Veeva. Education not listed.

founders.name: Jacob Caccamo
founders.role: Co-founder, COO and Head of Product
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: UX designer and front-end engineer focused on medical edtech, previously at NIH.

technical_complexity.rationale: Adaptive question banks, an AI tutor, curriculum mapping and LMS integration via LTI 1.3 are standard engineering with content creation as the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: School contracts with curriculum mapping and LMS integration create switching costs, and student performance data can compound, but established question banks such as UWorld are entrenched.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying the company; the site names UWorld as the benchmark in its own trial.

market_need_then: Medical schools care about licensing exam pass rates and attrition; the company states it serves 200 plus programs and 50,000 students, though these are self reported.

branding.domain_note: Uses oraai.com; ora.ai belongs to a different company.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical and results driven, citing trial pass rates

rebrands.why: Not stated; G2 and CB Insights say Ora AI was formerly Synaptiq, exact date unknown

branding.community_and_virality: Site shows student testimonials and quotes from Ross University School of Medicine and Penn Perelman School of Medicine.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is shared with several unrelated Ora companies and search finds little brand coverage, though testimonials suggest some student usage.

outcome_analysis: Ora AI is active and claims 200 plus schools and 50,000 students, built by a physician CEO with engineers from Block and Veeva. No funding round could be verified, so growth versus capital is unclear. The product sells to schools, which gives sticky revenue if the self reported usage holds.
notes: Round rests on a single database (CB Insights, listed under former name Synaptiq: about 500K over 2 rounds, seed dated 2023-07-01, Pioneer Fund and Y Combinator). Latka says the company is bootstrapped, a conflict; cross-check search found no press or filing, and the 500K figure also appears in unrelated SimCare AI coverage. Other companies named Ora (blockchain, Ora Computing) are unrelated. The company site claims a randomized trial with 100 percent first attempt Step 1 pass rate, self reported and not verified. No dated competitors found; results were 2026 comparison pages. The YC page references a separate YC listing for Synaptiq.
